DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http: //www.di'g.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 108 s. 2022 September 29, 2022 MR. CHRISTIAN LAWRENCE DULAY DE GUZMAN Brgy. Taal, City of Malolos, Bulacan christianlawrencedulaydeguzman@gmail.com Dear Mr. De Guzman. This has reference to your email dated 24 May 2022, 16 June 2022 and 8 August 2022 respectively, all requesting for assistance to the noise brought by the chatter of your neighbors and karaoke during the wee hours of the morning in Brgy- Taal, City of Malolos, Bulacan. In your email dated 24 May 2022 containing the aforementioned request, you maintained that you sent a Facebook message via messenger to your barangay captain but it was only read. Attached in the email were screenshots of messages sent to your profile including the Facebook profile links of the following (l ) facebook.com/renato.abalos.330, (2) facebook.com/barangay.taaI.39, and (3) facebook.com/sk.taal.18. While on your email dated 16 June 2022, your narration stated that you were accompanied by one Sangguniang Kabataan and a chief to reprimand the noisy neighbors yet the warning fell on deaf ears. In the same email, you also requested to apprehend and identify the names of the neighbors being complained of, but no action was taken on the matter. Further, you also mentioned that you signed a document but no further details were mentioned regarding this. In the end, the following are the requests mentioned in the aforementioned email: (1) safety of your family against the neighbors being complained of, (2) intermittent surveillance by the barangay of the place and the people involved in the noise, (3) adequate penalty for the people involved in this complaint; and (4) confidentiality of your complainant against the neighbors. Considering your allegations to the events which have transpired, our appreciation of the issues herein are : (I) whether there is/are basis/bases for filing a complaint against the neighbors; and (2) whether there is/are basis/bases for filing a complaint against the public official concerned. IJItimately, your request for the Department's assistance. Anent the first issue, may we refer your complaint to Kautusang Panglungsod Blg. 79- 2020 of Malolos Bulacan dated 5 October 2020 which states that: " xxx mahigpit na nagbabawal sa pagpapatugtog ng malakas ng mga videoke, karaoke o mga kahalintulad nito mula ika-7: 00 ng umaga hanggang ika-4: 00 ng hapon at mula ika-IO:OO ng gabi hanggang ika-7:OO ng umaga, mula Lunes "Matlno, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No,: 8876-34-54

hanggang Biyernes bilang bahagi sa pagsuporta sa 'home schooling' ng Kagawaran ng Edukasyon, pagpapataw ng kaparusahan hinggil dito at para sa iba pang layunuin." Further you can also file a complaint for unjust vexation pursuant to Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code of the Philippines, which is also defined by the Supreme Court in the case of Renato Baleros, Jr. vs. People of the Philippinesl as any human conduct, without violence, that unjustly annoys an innocent person, with the following elements: l. There is human conduct that unjustly annoys or irritates another person; 2. Such human conduct was not attended with violence; 3. Such human conduct caused annoyance, irritation, torment, distress or disturbance to the mind of the person to whom it is directed; and 4. Offender acted with criminal intent. With regard to the second issue, according to RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, the following are the powers, duties and functions of the local chief executive which can be found under Chapter III, Section 389, to wit: Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. - xxx xxx xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: (1) Enforce all laws and ordinances which are applicable within the barangay; xxx xxx (3) Maintain public order in the barangay and, in pursuance thereof, assist the city or municipal mayor and the sanggunian members in the performance of their duties and functions; xxx Clearly cited in the law is the obligation of the local chief executive to maintain the peace and order within his jurisdiction. Otherwise, a complaint may be filed against him/her as expressed in paragraph (c)Sec. 60 of RA 7160, to wit: dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty. [emphasis supplied], with the Sangguniang Panlungsod, in accordance with Section 612 thereof. Lastly, on the part of the Department, rest assured that we will take the necessary and appropriate action in dealing with your concern. 1 G.R. No. 138033 dated January 30, 2007 2 SECTION 61 , Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. — A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: xxx (c) A complaint against any elective barangay official shall be filed before the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory.XXX Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion issued by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTH ITY OF THE SEC TARY. VICTOR R. LLAMAS Unde e tary for External, Legal and Legislative Affai OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/rrao copy furnish: AITY ANTHONY C.
